name: GIAC Law of Data Security & Investigations

third_party_evaluations.summary: Legal/regulatory landscape for IR, e-discovery, evidence handling.

evaluation.rationale: Independent reviews of the stored evidence produced specialty: 3. The existing unordered-specialty rule applies when at least one reviewer identifies a specialty track. See each persona rationale for the supporting factors and limitations.

hiroshi-tanaka.rationale: Legal and evidence-handling coverage is a narrow advisory specialization supported by recorded accreditation; no experience requirement and a very specific use case do not map to general incident-response rank.

maria-okonkwo.rationale: Legal requirements for response, e-discovery and evidence handling form a narrow adjunct to operational security practice. Recorded accreditation and COOL recognition help assurance, but zero listed experience and a knowledge exam do not establish general practitioner seniority.

alex-novak.rationale: Legal issues in incident response, e-discovery and evidence handling form the recorded narrow supporting discipline. The specialty hint is appropriate without treating legal knowledge as a higher general technical rank.
